evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: strips curl base-first, with rows 3 to 6 bent into arcs and hooks while the top two rows stay upright; by shot-20s the open-to-closed diagonal shows the wave has moved across the grid.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: 48 segmented strips, each with pale skin and dark fiber lines, plus ochre rounded haze tiles behind every strip; shot-20s: the camera has pulled back to a cream margin around the grid.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: cream radial ground with ochre edges, rust-to-graphite strips and dark bases match the stated palette; shot-08s: an uneven gap at column five and small strips leave a lot of empty cream.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: a pine-cone scale bending as a segmented grid is not a textbook bilayer or a plasma cliche; shot-20s: rust arcs against ochre tiles, unlike the flock or bar-chart anchors.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: upright, symmetric grid composed at the start; shot-20s: strips resolve into a diagonal open-to-closed gradient that differs from 2 s, but the frame is small and the caption sits in the corner.

pairwise_justification: No median archive yet exists, so there is no head-to-head comparison to make.

critique.change: Make the grid spacing uniform: column five shows an irregular gap at shot-08s and shot-20s. Use an even pitch so the wave reads as one field.
Scale the grid up so the strips fill more of the frame at shot-02s and shot-20s, letting the curl read at full size instead of small arcs in cream space.

Show the skin-versus-fiber split and the open-close path on screen: darken the fiber face on the curled strips and add a faint per-strip angle trace at shot-20s, so the hysteresis is seen rather than captioned.
